subject: SIG: telemetry samples + KMS proof for dataflow
messages:
From: Alex Graves <alex.graves@starlitecapital.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Narang <priya.narang@starlitecapital.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: Clarify telemetry samples + KMS proof for dataflow

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the questionnaire. We are running through Redwood's SIG and have a couple of follow-ups before we complete the control mapping:

1) Telemetry/logging: can you send a small redacted sample of runtime request/response logs that demonstrates the fields you capture (timestamps, model id, route, latency, error codes)? We only need samples — not full archives — but they should include an example of a request that hits a cached prefix and one that does not.

2) KMS evidence: we need a description and proof materials that show how customer encryption keys are handled (wrapping, rotation events, and whether Redwood stores plaintext at rest). A signed statement or an exported KMS audit entry would work.

3) Dataflow diagram: a simple diagram or bullet list showing how request data flows from API -> runtime -> cache -> storage (where applicable) and which components see plaintext.

For timeline, procurement is asking for these artifacts by COB Friday 8/13 so we can include them in our assurance package. If you need a sampling window or format constraints for the logs, let us know.

Appreciate the quick turn — Priya and I will review as soon as we have the artifacts.

Best,
Alex
Security & Risk Manager
Starlite Capital

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: Clarify telemetry samples + KMS proof for dataflow

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for; below is what I propose and a quick clarification question so we size the artifacts correctly.

Proposed deliverables (we will redacts PII and tokens):
- Two redacted telemetry snippets (JSON log lines): one cache-hit flow, one cold-path flow; will include model id, route, request/response timing, and an obfuscated request_id.
- KMS proof: export of key-wrap events from our KMS audit logs (timestamped), plus a short attestation from our Security Engineer describing rotation cadence and whether we ever hold plaintext.
- Dataflow summary: a one-page diagram (PNG) and a bullet list that maps which services see plaintext and which only see ciphertext.

Clarification: when you say "sample size," do you prefer a handful of lines (~20 each) or a single session trace with correlated spans? We can do either; correlated session traces are more useful for latency and cache-hit examples.

I will upload the artifacts to the evidence portal and share the Drive folder link. Attaching our evidence intake instructions for format/PII redaction: redwood-soc2-evidence-instructions.pdf

If that works, Vanessa will produce the KMS export and Karthik can pull the session traces. We can aim to get the first bundle to you by Thurs 8/12 EOD.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security & Trust Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: Clarify telemetry samples + KMS proof for dataflow

Alex/Priya — quick notes on the KMS piece:

- Redwood supports two customer key modes: managed (Redwood KMS) and BYOK (customer-managed keys). For BYOK we only have wrapped keys and we do not retain plaintext. The attached attestation will explicitly state that.
- For the KMS export, we can provide HSM/KMS audit events showing wrap/unwrap operations (timestamps and operation type) — we will redact any sensitive ARNs but keep operation ids for traceability.
- Rotation: default rotation is every 90 days for managed keys; for BYOK rotation is customer-driven — we will note which mode is used on your account.

Drive link for artifacts (will populate once uploads are ready): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-evidence

We usually provide ~25 log lines per scenario (cache-hit, cache-miss), each with correlated span ids. If you'd rather get a single end-to-end trace for a handful of requests, say so and we'll provide that.

Vanessa Ortiz
Trust & Risk Ops
Redwood Inference

2) Fri 8/13 AM: Vanessa will deliver the KMS audit export and a two-paragraph attestation about rotation/plaintext handling.
3) Mon 8/16: live 20-min demo of evidence portal + walkthrough of a redacted session trace (we can do 10–10:30am PT).

We will include: request_id, model_id (redacted), route, timestamp, latency_ms, cache_hit boolean, and an obfuscated request_payload_hash. The log lines will be JSON and the session trace will be a small zipped trace bundle.

Attaching the redacted sample we plan to upload so you can confirm the format: telemetry-sample-2027-07-redacted.log

If that timeline is tight, we can compress and push the KMS export earlier.
